From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO measurement & evidence requirements for RFP

Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short playbook and an SLO matrix that cover our standard measurement definitions plus two optional modes (Hosted and Private). Key highlights up front:
- Availability: default is rolling 24-hour windows aligned to UTC for calculation; monthly aggregation uses calendar-month UTC windows unless the customer requests local-calendar windows in the contract.
- Latency: we compute p50/p95/p99 from sampled production traces at 1s resolution with stratified sampling by region and route. For global customers we compute per-region percentiles and a weighted global view (weight = region rps over the month).
- Partial degradations: credits are prorated by impacted RPS and weighted by the proportion of requests that hit the affected region or model variant. Sample calculation included.

I attached: redwood-slo-playbook-v2.pdf (playbook), aurora_slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO targets mapped to routes).

Propose a 60-minute technical workshop with your SRE + our infra SLA owners to walk the measurement artifacts and confirm adjudication owners — are you available Thursday 10–11am PT?

Rafael
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-slo-playbook-v2.pdf, aurora_slo_matrix.xlsx

Sanjay —

Following Rafael's summary, a few clarifications from the instrumentation and adjudication side that should address the procurement questions and help your legal & SRE teams:

1) Metering sources (primary/secondary)
   - Primary: ingest-side telemetry (edge/ingress) and internal outbound probe fleet (hosted customers). These are our authoritative sources for availability and latency.
   - Secondary: customer-side synthetic probes (if provided) and the control-plane request logs. Secondary sources are used for reconciliation but not for unilateral credit calculation unless contractually agreed.

2) Windowing and rounding
   - We measure availability on rolling 24h windows with a monthly aggregation used for credit triggers. Sub-minute outages are rounded to the nearest second; availability percentages are reported to three decimal places.

3) Sampling methodology for latency
   - Stratified sampling at 1s resolution with per-route reservoir sampling to preserve tail accuracy. For low-volume routes (<1 req/min), we fall back to full-sample on a 24h rolling buffer.

4) Multi-region weighting and partial-degradation example
   - Example: If Region A carries 60% of monthly RPS and observes p99 latency breaching the target for a 4h window while Region B is normal, the credit applied = (impacting RPS share) * (duration fraction) * (credit_factor). See attached worked example and a CSV formula stub.

5) Adjudication and appeals workflow
   - First pass: automated detection (Redwood telemetry) and provisional credit calculation.
   - Customer-initiated appeal within 14 days with evidence bundle (logs, synthetic probes).
   - Final adjudication with both parties' telemetry owners; disputed evidence is reconciled within 7 business days.

6) Private deployment notes
   - For VPC/on-prem we ship a probe pack and recommended probe topology; if customer opts to host probes we provide a reference implementation and guidance on probe placement. Hosted probe telemetry remains the default authoritative source unless otherwise specified in SOW.

Attachments: SLO-adjudication-worked-example.csv, measurement-runbook-exec-summary.pdf

If this looks aligned I can draft the short runbook for legal ops that maps evidence owners to contract statements. Rafael — happy to join the call if we lock the time.

—Laura
Senior Product Manager, Observability — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO measurement & evidence requirements for RFP

Sanjay — thanks, and great to get this into a short decision path. Operational/legal notes from our side: 

- Billing time-zone option: we can support customer-requested calendar windows (America/Chicago) as a contract-level option for year one. We'll include a clause that specifies the measurement anchor and conversion rules.

- Service credit formula (example):
   credit = max(0, ((target_availability - observed_availability) / target_availability) * monthly_commitment * prorate_factor) * impacted_weight
   - rounding: credits rounded up to the next whole dollar for payouts below $5k; larger credits processed as invoices/credits per standard billing cycle.

- Dispute evidence: Redwood will provide a pull-based evidence bundle (telemetry snapshot + relevant probe traces) available for 30 days post-incident; retention extensions are available as an add-on.

- Next steps:
   1) Rafael to send calendar invite for Thu 2027-09-10 10:00–11:00 PT with a one-page pre-read for Legal Ops (Rafael: can you include the sample CSV and short runbook?).
   2) Laura to prepare the adjudication runbook and evidence checklist for the workshop.
   3) Procurement to share any template clauses they require prior to the session.

Attached: service-credit-formula.csv (worked calculations), redwood-legal-ops-preRead.pdf (one-pager).

Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Operations — Redwood Inference
